title: CVE-2023-28320: siglongjmp race condition
excerpt:
## Summary:
If the system has no POSIX or Windows threading support, `USE_ALARM_TIMEOUT` codepath will be used in `lib/hostip.c`. If two threads will perform DNS resolving, a wrong register context can be used on  the signal handler`siglongjmp` call if DNS timeout occurs. Typically this results in segmentation fault, but depending on platform specifics other impacts might be possible (but unlikely).

The documentation warns against this very issue in https://curl.se/libcurl/c/threadsafe.html `It is important that libcurl can find and use thread safe versions of these and other system calls, as otherwise it cannot function fully thread safe.` The issue is that there is no way for the application using libcurl to know if the library is MT safe for DNS resolution or not. `CURL_VERSION_THREADSAFE` is mentioned, but this checks availability of atomic init, not MT safety of DNS resolution.

A remote attacker in a privileged network position is able to selectively block the DNS responses and may thus induce the affected target application to crash.

## Steps To Reproduce:

  1. For quick testing on POSIX systems add `#define USE_ALARM_TIMEOUT` to `lib/hostip.c`, for example:
 ```
diff --git a/lib/hostip.c b/lib/hostip.c
index 2381290fd..0148f2861 100644
--- a/lib/hostip.c
+++ b/lib/hostip.c
@@ -75,6 +75,7 @@
 /* alarm-based timeouts can only be used with all the dependencies satisfied */
 #define USE_ALARM_TIMEOUT
 #endif
+#define USE_ALARM_TIMEOUT

 #define MAX_HOSTCACHE_LEN (255 + 7) /* max FQDN + colon + port number + zero */

 ```
  2. Compile libcurl
  3. Compile version of https://curl.se/libcurl/c/multithread.html but add `curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_TIMEOUT, 2);` to  `pull_one_url` function.
  4. Change DNS config to point to blackhole DNS server at `3.219.212.117` (blackhole.webpagetest.org)
  5. Execute the compiled `multithread` and the application will segfault.

summary: A race condition in the USE_ALARM_TIMEOUT codepath of lib/hostip.c can cause a segmentation fault during concurrent DNS resolution, potentially leading to denial of service.

claims.text: siglongjmp race condition when multiple threads perform DNS resolving in USE_ALARM_TIMEOUT codepath
claims.reasoning: The USE_ALARM_TIMEOUT codepath uses a global sigjmp_buf (curl_jmpenv) at line 915 with no locking. Multiple threads calling Curl_resolv_timeout concurrently will overwrite each other's jump buffer. When a SIGALRM fires, siglongjmp uses whichever thread's context was last stored, causing a crash.

key_reasons: Global curl_jmpenv used without locking in USE_ALARM_TIMEOUT codepath (lib/hostip.c:915)
Comment at line 912 acknowledges known problems with this technique
Multiple threads overwrite each other's sigsetjmp context, causing siglongjmp to jump to wrong stack frame
Attacker in privileged network position can induce DNS timeouts to trigger the race
Results in segmentation fault (denial of service)
GLOBAL_INIT_IS_THREADSAFE and curl_simple_lock_lock exist but are not used to protect this codepath
reply: Thank you for the detailed report. The race condition in the USE_ALARM_TIMEOUT codepath is confirmed: lib/hostip.c:915 uses global curl_jmpenv without any locking, and the comment at line 912 acknowledges known problems. Multiple threads doing DNS resolution with timeouts will overwrite each other's jump buffer, causing siglongjmp to jump to an invalid context and crash. This is a valid denial-of-service issue reachable by an attacker who can block DNS responses. The fix should add locking around the USE_ALARM_TIMEOUT section when GLOBAL_INIT_IS_THREADSAFE is available, as you proposed.
